name: Detect decaying WordPress posts in Search Console and generate AI refresh briefs with OpenAI and Google Sheets

parameters.content:
## Detect decaying WordPress posts in Search Console and get AI refresh briefs

### How it works

Every Monday this workflow compares the last 28 days of Google Search Console data with the 28 days before and flags pages whose clicks dropped past your threshold. They are ranked by clicks lost. For each page it compares **queries one by one** to see which ones lost clicks and which new ones appeared, pulls the **full article from WordPress** (or the live HTML for non-WordPress URLs), and an LLM writes a refresh brief: diagnosis, likely causes, concrete actions, new sections to add and a suggested title. Briefs land in Google Sheets as `pending`.

**It also measures the result.** When you finish rewriting a page, set its `status` to `refreshed`. The next run stamps today's date in `refreshed_at` (or keeps the date you typed). Once 28 days of post-refresh data exist, it compares clicks in the 28 days before and after the refresh, writes `clicks_before`, `clicks_after` and `refresh_result`, and sets `status` to `measured`.

### Setup steps

- **Search Console:** create a **Google OAuth2 API** credential with scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly` and select it in the five Search Console HTTP nodes.
- **Google Sheets:** create a tab named `Refresh Log` with this header row:
`page_url | wp_id | wp_type | last_modified | clicks_prev | clicks_now | click_change | lost_clicks | position_prev | position_now | lost_queries | new_queries | priority | diagnosis | actions | new_sections | suggested_title | status | detected_at | refreshed_at | clicks_before | clicks_after | refresh_result`
- **WordPress:** create an Application Password and a WordPress API credential for the three WordPress nodes. Read-only access is enough. This workflow never writes to your site.
- **AI model:** add OpenAI credentials, or swap the chat model for Claude, Gemini or another model.
- **Config:** set `gsc_property` (e.g. `sc-domain:example.com` or `https://example.com/`), `wp_base_url`, `sheet_id` and `language`.
- Run **Manual Workflow Trigger** once with `max_per_run = 2` and check the sheet.

### Sheet statuses

`pending` → you rewrite the page → `refreshed` → measured automatically → `measured`. Use `skipped` to dismiss a brief. Pages with an open brief are never re-flagged, and others wait `cooldown_days`.

### Customization

- `drop_threshold` (0.3 = clicks down 30% or more) and `min_prev_clicks` control sensitivity.
- `compare_days` sets both the comparison window and the measurement window.
- `max_article_chars` limits how much article text is sent to the LLM (cost control).
- Add a Slack or email node after **Add Refresh Brief to Sheets** to get a weekly digest.

## Start and configure

Provides scheduled and manual entry points, then sets the shared workflow parameters used by Search Console, WordPress, AI, and Sheets steps.

## Load refresh log

Reads the existing Google Sheets refresh log, which feeds both the new-brief generation path and the refresh tracking path.

## Detect decaying pages

Fetches current and previous Search Console page performance, then flags URLs whose clicks dropped enough to require a content refresh brief.

## Match WordPress records

Looks up decaying URLs against WordPress posts and pages by slug, then matches each URL to a WordPress ID and content type where possible.

## Compare query changes

Retrieves current and previous Search Console query data for each matched page and calculates which search queries gained, lost, or need attention.

## Build article context

Branches based on whether a WordPress match exists, fetching either the WordPress article record or the live page HTML, then converts the content into prompt-ready headings and plain text.

## Generate AI brief

Uses an OpenAI chat model and structured output parser within the LLM chain to produce a refresh brief from the performance changes and article context.

## Save generated brief

Formats the AI output with page metadata and appends the finished refresh brief to Google Sheets for editorial review.

## Classify refresh status

Processes existing sheet rows to find items marked as refreshed, decides whether each is ready for measurement, and stamps a refresh date when needed.

## Measure refresh impact

For rows ready to evaluate, fetches Search Console clicks around the refresh date, calculates before-versus-after performance, and saves the measured result back to Google Sheets.
